subject: Model selection: plot-level covarite vs survey-level covariate models

messages.author: ab435006c4cbbde3
messages.subject: Model selection: plot-level covarite vs survey-level covariate models
parts:
Hi all,
I am technically new to occupancy models and new to unmarked. I have a dataset of Leporidae data, 115 sites with a maximum of 4 surveys per site. Not all plots got to be surveyed four times, though (See the following screenshot), and one plot did not get to be surveyed at all.

Moreover, I have survey-level covariates and plot-level covariates. I am trying to model the detection probability, so I fit models with one covariate each, some at the plot level and others at the survey level. This is the warning message I am getting when using a survey level covariate, which I think makes sense given how the dataset looks like:

Here is the warning message that I get for the models with a covariate at the plot level, which I think also makes sense since one plot did not get surveyed at all:


When trying to build the fitList() to be used in modSel I get errors that prevent R from creating the fitList. Could you explain why I can compare models that use covariates at different levels? I can only compare between all the models with survey-level covariates or between all models with plot-level covariates.
Thanks!
~Airy

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Model selection: plot-level covarite vs survey-level covariate models
parts:
In order to compare models they need to be all using identical datasets. If you have missing values in a covariate, then parts of the dataset will be dropped to accomdate this, resulting in a different dataset than if you had not included that covariate. So model with covariate vs model without covariate will not have the same dataset, hence the error.

This can be difficult to solve depending on the exact arrangement of missing values. As the message suggests you should try to create one common dataset with all the relevant missing values removed already (manually), and then fit all models using this common dataset.

Ken
